title: Front-of-Pack Labeling: FDA's Proposed Nutrition Information Rule
excerpt: The FDA has proposed mandatory front-of-package nutrition labels requiring a 'Nutrition Info box' displaying Low, Med, or High interpretive ratings for saturated fat, sodium, and added sugars on most packaged foods. Published January 16, 2025, the rule received 11,000+ comments and could be finalized in spring 2026 — though the Trump administration's MAHA initiative may reshape the final design.
seo_title: FDA Front-of-Pack Labeling Rule: Proposed Requirements & Timeline | Policy Canary
seo_description: Complete regulatory intelligence on the FDA's proposed front-of-pack nutrition labeling rule (21 CFR 101). Covers the Nutrition Info box design, Low/Med/High thresholds, comment period timeline, MAHA implications, international FOP systems, and what food manufacturers should do to prepare.

key_deadlines.label: Proposed rule published in Federal Register

structured_data.compliance_timeline: 3 years after final rule ($10M+ businesses), 4 years (under $10M)
